rationale: The two solutions use the same logic: the same state, the same check that raises ValueError once the game has ended, the same rule that a wrong or repeated letter costs a guess, and the same win/lose checks and masked-word output. Neither is more robust than the other. Neither validates its input (for example, single lowercase characters), and both count a repeated wrong letter as another failure. B is slightly more readable in three small ways. Its comment states the rule that a repeated correct letter counts as a failure, which a reader would not guess. It moves the win condition into a well-named helper, _all_letters_guessed, so the end-of-turn check reads like the rules of the game. It uses the name char instead of the single letter c. These changes add almost no complexity, so B wins by a small margin on clarity.
